claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder can be pre-coated with nanoscale Y2O3 using resonant acoustic mixing.
The Y2O3 coating forms a uniform layer on the powder particles.
Y2O3-coated powder can be consolidated by LPBF into dense components.
The initial AlCrFeNiSi powder is gas-atomized and has standard morphology and flow properties.
The coated AlCrFeNiSi powder should be processed using reduced LPBF energy-density settings.
Reduced LPBF energy density minimizes high thermal input.
Mechanical tests are to be conducted at room temperature under quasi-static loading.
The oxide particles remain dispersed throughout the LPBF build volume.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles provide dispersion strengthening.
Y2O3 dispersoids produce a finer and more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure during rapid solidification.
Nanoscale oxide dispersoids act as pinning centers during solidification.
Oxide-particle pinning reduces grain growth.
Oxide dispersoids limit the development of thermal gradients during LPBF.
Limiting thermal gradients mitigates residual-stress accumulation.
Oxide-coated AlCrFeNiSi parts will have lower residual thermal stresses than uncoated parts made under conventional high-thermal-load LPBF conditions.
Oxide-coated AlCrFeNiSi parts will have a more refined microstructure than the conventional high-thermal-load baseline.
Oxide-coated parts will exhibit higher strength than the uncoated baseline.
Oxide-coated parts will exhibit higher ductility than the uncoated baseline.
The hypothesis is limited to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components fabricated by LPBF.
Effects under other additive-manufacturing techniques or substantially different component scales remain unverified.

contradictions.description: The treatment is specified as using reduced-energy-density LPBF while the baseline uses conventional high-thermal-load LPBF, but the falsification experiment says all processing parameters are identical except for powder coating. These designs cannot simultaneously isolate the coating intervention and compare reduced-energy treatment processing against a high-thermal-load baseline.
